Wednesday, October 7th, 12:03 AM

My eyes flashed open, my heart startling. It felt like I had just fallen on the bed. I heard a loud THUD from the other room. Cautiously, my chest beginning to hurt from the hyperventilation, I tossed my robe over my naked body and grabbed my phone. I clicked on the flashlight, stepping cautiously on the creaky wooden floor.

My heavy pocket doors were partially open. Strange. I thought I closed them. I jumped as I felt something brush against the side of my leg, looking down, I see my pleasantly plump cat trotting into my bedroom. He mewed at me, licked my leg and continued to his bowl of water.

"Dammit, Meeko, did you open the door?" I asked, as if he would answer. He just stared at me and mewed for more food. I closed the door, satisfied with the idea my cat somehow wiggled through the door and caused the noise. I crawled back in bed, and pulled the covers up. He soon joined me, his not so graceful self landing on my stomach, his paws pressing pretty hard on my breasts.

"Get off me, ya idiot!" I held him close and petted him until we were almost asleep. He purred softly in my ear, occasionally attempting to lick my hair. I was grateful to have such a gentle and loving cat. He never hissed, never bit, only excessively wanted cuddles. Then I heard the thud again.

It was closer this time. I startled up. Meeko bolted upright, his tail puffy. Another thud. My eyes widened as I fumbled for my phone. I turned on my flashlight app again. I swore I saw a shadow. I got out of bed and ran to the standing lamp, turned it on -- nothing. Time to be brave, I guessed.

I exited the room, wishing I had a better, less ridiculous weapon than a decorative sword and a practice bow. I got to the kitchen, flipping on every light in the apartment. A few cups were knocked over. I grabbed a kitchen knife, putting down my ridiculous weapon of choice, and slightly chuckled at how that would look. I double checked all of the doors and windows -- all still locked with the little chain on them. Nothing seemed to be wrong except for those cups. Meeko probably knocked them down a little, and the rest now just started to fall. Yeah, that made sense.

Leaving the lights on, I decided to bunk up on the couch. Seemed less scary. I turned on Robin Hood: Men In Tights for a bit of laughs and covered up with blankets again, with Meeko curled up beside me. It was nearly 2:45 am. Drifting off to sleep once more, there were no more thuds. I closed my eyes, shifted onto my stomach, wanting desperately to just stay asleep for longer than a few minutes. That's when I felt it. Breath on the back of my neck. And then... The Voice. That horrible Voice.

"You're already dead."

I jumped awake, screaming, I turned around, a shadowy figure of a man fleeting out the door. Meeko was hissing. He never hissed. I grabbed him, my phone, the knife, and the blanket and locked myself in the bathroom. I called 911.

"Jefferson County 911, where is your emergency?"

I gave my address.

"What is the emergency?"

"There was someone in my house!" I was hyperventilating. I barely could make the words out as my throat choked on fear and tears. "H-he said "You're already dead" and then ran off."

"Ma'am do you live with anyone else?"

"Yes, but they're in Chicago for the week... there was someone in here, I need help! Please!"

"Okay, Police are on the way, Can you stay on the line with me?"

"Yes, please hurry." I managed to squeak out.

"Of course honey, what's your name?" the operator's voice was soothing, clear, and polite.

"Eleanor Marie Blanchett." I responded, in hushed tones.

"Where are you in your house right now?"

"I locked myself in my bathroom."

"Do you have any weapons?"

"I took a kitchen knife from the block... it's on me."

"Can you tell me again what happened?"

It carried on like this for some time. I repeated my night over and over again. I knew I saw someone, the security cameras outside would get the footage and prove me right. I knew they would. The police arrived, combed the apartment. Four officers. It seemed a lot for a standard house call. One of the officers sat down at my kitchen table across from me and began writing my information down. Meeko was calming down, trying to get on the officer's lap. The officer smiled and helped him up.

"Cute cat. You sure your shadow wasn't just him?" He looked up at me. I'm not certain if it was concern or patronizing pity in his eyes, but he was somehow calming.

"I'm sure, Officer... um..."

"Johnson. Alright Miss Blanchett, can I call you Eleanor?"

"Ellie," I responded. I don't know why I did.

"Ellie, alright, I'll be right back. The guys are looking over the security footage right now. I'll be right in the other room."

He left me. I could still see him, though. Another officer was speaking to him and a female officer in hushed tones, his back turned to me so I couldn't even read his lips. I saw Officer Johnson's face turn into a frown. He nodded, and walked back toward me. The other officers watched as he walked to me.

"Ellie, have you taken anything tonight?" He asked, jotting down the questions and answers in his notepad.

"No, sir. I had a glass of wine at dinner, but that's all." I held my blanket closer around me.

"And do you take any medications for sleep, anxiety, depression, or any anti-psychotics?"

I looked at him, confused.

"No, sir. I don't take any of those."

"Alright. Well, I don't know how to tell you, but there wasn't anything on the camera. Have you slept at all?"

"What, no... that's not right I saw something and It was RIGHT there! It spoke to me and -" I curled up on the ground sobbing. Johnson put his hand on my shoulder.

"Hey, Ellie? Hey... It's me, Officer Johnson..." Why was he speaking to me like that? "You know sometimes when you don't sleep for a long time, you begin to hallucinate. It sometimes feels very real, and sometimes you can even hear things you normally wouldn't."

I nodded, sniffling. I clutched Meeko close to my chest. He purred. He was my best friend. I thought I almost lost him once, but he made a miraculous recovery.

"Yeah, I haven't slept more than an hour a night for the past week or so."

Officer Johnson nodded again. He sat with me until I began to breathe normally again. The pains in my sides from hyperventilation made it hurt to inhale, but it returned to normal. Shaking, white hot tears kept springing to my eyes. I felt like a moron.

There I was, a 23 year old who got scared, called the cops, all over a nightmare. I was humiliated. Another officer approached. Johnson nodded at me as I looked up at her, clutching Meeko. She was pretty, her large, glassy blue eyes filled with concern. I could see myself in them. I looked like a mess.

"Hey, Ellie? I'm Officer Schmidt. I looked through your phone and called your Dad. He was listed as ICE. He'll be over shortly, okay? We can stay with you while you get an overnight bag, talk with him as to what we think's going on, and then he'll take you home, okay, sweetheart?"

I burst into tears again. I was so confused. And scared. And humiliated. She had to call my dad.

"Hey, Ellie?" Officer Johnson piped up, "Look, this doesn't make you weak or anything. I used to go through it a lot when I was about your age. I got better, and it doesn't seem like it right now, but it will. I'm sure Meeko will be right here with you too, won't you boy?"

Meeko meowed in agreement.

"And hey, if you ever need me, this is my house phone, okay? Call me anytime you need me." I clutched the bit of paper he handed me to my chest and hugged him.

"Thanks, Officer."

I came out in the living room. Dad was there with my step mom. Dad ran up and hugged me.

"Hey, punk."

"Hey daddy."

"It's gonna be okay. I'll help you with your bags." Dad took my bag from me. My step mom was staring at Meeko.

"Why are you--" Dad cut her off by shaking his head. He whispered something in her ear and she nodded. She smiled at me.

"Okay, Ellie, let's get you settled. The officers are gonna stay back a bit longer. Just gonna look a few things over. We gave them the key to lock up."

I nodded and toted Meeko and myself to the back of the oversized SUV.

That was the first night.

Over the next few weeks, I became somewhat of a recluse. Dad enrolled me in therapy, and I would go straight back to my room at their house and curl up with Meeko. I thought I was responding well to treatment.

It is Tuesday, October 27th now. I came downstairs. Dad was crying. I guess they didn't hear me.

"She's just carrying on pretending that damn cat is still alive. She feeds him, changes the litter box, gives him water... he's not even there."

My heart lept to my throat. What did he mean Meeko was dead? I just was cuddling him. Officer Johnson saw him, too. No, maybe I misheard...

"She asks me to watch him when she goes to therapy, and I can't take it anymore, Laura. She's so fucked up and seein' things that aren't there. I want my baby girl back."

I crept back to my room, tears in my eyes again. I never saw dad break down. Not even once. I looked at Meeko, who hopped up on the bed.

"You're real, right, buddy?" Meeko forced his head between my arms and curled up. I remembered the number Will had given me.

I fumbled around, looking for the scrap paper. At long last, I found it. I picked up my cell and began punching in the numbers.

Ring. Ring.

I hoped he wouldn't be too mad at me. It was nearly midnight.

Ring. Ring.

"Hello?" A woman's voice answered. It must be his wife.

"Hello, Ma'am, um, I'm a friend of Will's... can I please speak with him?"

"...Excuse me?" her voice cracked.

"I'm sorry to call so late, he helped me out a few weeks ago, and told me to call him if I had any more questions -- I'm sorry it's so late, I can call back another --"

"...I think you don't understand. Will... passed on the 6th of October." I could hear her sobs echoing through the phone.

My heart sunk.

Click. The call ended. Logged. It was real...right?

I looked over where Meeko sat, playing on the bed. Behind him, the shadow.

I don't know what's real anymore.
